housing.summary: Numbeo reports £886.33 per month for a one-bedroom apartment in Belfast city centre, last updated 1 September 2026: https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/in/Belfast Northern Ireland caps a private-tenancy deposit at one month's rent: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/tenancy-deposit-scheme-information-tenants PropertyPal describes itself as NI's favourite property portal with the most NI listings: https://www.propertypal.com/mobile-apps

banking.summary: Bank of Ireland UK's Clear Account application requires valid photo ID and proof of address; applicants not living in the UK also need their latest three months of current-bank statements: https://www.bankofirelanduk.com/personal/current-account/clear-account/
required_docs: latest three months of current-bank statements if not living in the UK

schools.summary: Belfast schools follow the statutory Northern Ireland Curriculum across 12 years of compulsory education: https://www.education-ni.gov.uk/articles/statutory-curriculum The Department of Education's Schools Plus service is the official institutions directory: https://www.education-ni.gov.uk/services/schools-plus

legal_admin.summary: A newcomer with UK immigration permission needs a UKVI account to access an eVisa; after creating the account they must confirm identity and link the account to the eVisa: https://www.gov.uk/evisa/set-up-ukvi-account
legal_admin.registration_step: Create or access a UKVI account, confirm identity, and link it to the eVisa if not already linked

tax_finance.summary: Apply online for a National Insurance number and prove identity; a passport or eligible national identity card can be used, while applicants without those documents may need an in-person identity appointment: https://www.gov.uk/apply-national-insurance-number/how-to-apply

transport.summary: Translink's Belfast Metro and Glider Smartlink adult one-month unlimited travel card costs £63, plus a £1 initial card charge: https://www.translink.co.uk/tickets/travelcards/multi-journey-travelcards/metro-glider-smartlink Licence exchange depends on issuing country: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/exchanging-your-foreign-driving-licence Newcomers should register with a GP immediately using form HSCR-1: https://online.hscni.net/access-health-social-care/
transport.driving_licence_exchange: A valid EU/EEA Group 1 licence may be used until it expires. A valid licence from a designated country or region may be used for one year after becoming resident in Northern Ireland and exchanged within five years; apply within 12 months for continuous driving entitlement. https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/exchanging-your-foreign-driving-licence
transport.healthcare_registration: Register with a local GP straight away after arriving in Northern Ireland and complete form HSCR-1; a medical card is issued after registration. https://online.hscni.net/access-health-social-care/
